guide: Open the Start sheet and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: margin target, thin margin, callback target, close rate, warranty reserve, overhead a month and the extras on pay (confirm with your adviser).
Check Job types and Technicians. They hold your target margin for each job type (a typical range, check your own numbers) and the hourly rate of each technician; the other sheets read them.
Check the Price book: the fixed price per task, built from cost, with its labour hours, parts and all-in cost. Jobs are compared with it.
Enter every finished job on Jobs: price, hours on site, helper hours, drive hours and each cost line. Total cost, margin, margin percent and a one-line verdict fill in by themselves.
Use Job costing lines to see the cost lines of any job and the share of the price that parts and labour take.
Write each return visit to fix the same job on Callbacks (a callback), linked to the original job, with hours, parts and cost. Who paid and the share of the original price calculate.
Type the totals of the last 120 days for each job type on Margin by job type. Trend, gap to target, the price rise needed and margin per hour calculate.
Keep Ticket by month, Ticket by technician, Ticket by van and Ticket by site type up to date. The average ticket is the amount billed on one job.
Callback rate by technician and by job type read the Callbacks sheet; Callback reasons shows which cause costs most.
Watch Water heater margin: the margin against the target month by month and the unit cost rise after a supplier price change.
Type your own numbers on Repair or replace; the sentence for the estimate calculates. It gives no technical advice.
Use Scenario table and the What-if tool to test labour, parts and close rate (estimates won over estimates decided) on monthly profit.
Use the 18 tools, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Job Costing Dashboard and Charts every week: margin, ticket, losing jobs, callbacks, warranty cost and water heater margin.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Job Costing Excel Template: Job Margin, Callbacks, Warranty Cost, Price Book, Repair or Replace
listing.headline: See what every job really earned, by job type and technician
listing.description:
Job costing for a small HVAC and plumbing contractor in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-run service shop with one to fifteen technicians, an office manager who dispatches and a few vans. Jobs holds every finished job with its price and each cost line: parts, labour, permit, disposal, subcontract and vehicle. Total cost, margin, margin percent against the price book and a one-line verdict (won money, thin margin, lost money because of parts, hours, price or a callback) fill in by themselves.

Margin by job type compares the last 120 days of all 15 job types with their own targets, with the 12 months before and with the same days last year, and works out the price rise needed to reach the target. Water Heater Margin shows the margin month by month against the target after a supplier price rise. Ticket sheets give the average ticket (the amount billed on one job) and margin by technician, van, site type and month.

Callbacks links every return visit to fix the same job to the original job, with hours, parts, travel and cost, and shows who paid. Callback rate by technician and by job type, callback reasons, callback-aware margin and a warranty cost tracker show where money leaks. Repair or replace turns your own age, quote, price and life numbers into a cost per year of each choice and a plain sentence for the estimate.

18 tools answer weekly questions: which jobs lost money, which job type to re-price first, what labour or parts prices do to monthly profit, and what the next weeks may earn. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to customers, landlord accounts, technicians, the office manager, the owner, suppliers, subcontractors and the accountant.

This is part three of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no per-technician fee, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. It helps you keep track of your own numbers and does not promise results.

competitors.what: field-service app with a per-technician fee
competitors.lacks: bills every seat each month and shows job totals, but not the cost lines of one job, margin by job type against your target or callback cost
records what you billed and nothing about what the job cost, so a job that lost money looks the same as one that made money
prices one job from a markup but never checks the result against hours, parts, permit and subcontract cost after the job is done
keeps hours and parts on paper, with no margin per job, no callback rate by technician and no warning when a supplier price rise eats a job type
reports profit by month but cannot rank losing jobs, price the rise needed per job type or tell a callback from a new job

paragraphs: Repair or replace summary from {set:company}, dated {today}. Site {col:replace_inputs.site_ref}, quote date {col:replace_inputs.quote_date}. Equipment: {col:replace_inputs.equip_type}, {col:replace_inputs.age_years} years old; expected life used in this summary: {col:replace_inputs.life_years} years.

Repair quote: {col:replace_inputs.repair_quote}. Replacement price: {col:replace_inputs.replace_price}. Repair per remaining year: {col:replace_inputs.repair_year}. Replacement per year: {col:replace_inputs.replace_year}.
In plain words: {col:replace_inputs.sentence}. These are our own numbers and not a technical opinion. Please check with us before you decide.
The choice of the customer and the date are written below.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business and check your own local rules.

documents.title: Price correction proposal for one job type
paragraphs: Price correction proposal of {set:company}, dated {today}. Job type {col:margin_jt.job_type}.
Today the price per job is {col:margin_jt.price_job} and the cost per job is {col:margin_jt.cost_job}, so the margin is {col:margin_jt.margin_pct_120} against a target of {col:margin_jt.target}.

The price per job for the target is {col:margin_jt.price_target}, a rise of {col:margin_jt.rise_target}. With the buffer the rise would be {col:margin_jt.rise_buffer}, and at this pace of {col:margin_jt.jobs_year} jobs a year it recovers {col:margin_jt.recover_year} a year before any jobs are lost.
Decision, new flat price and start date are written below.

documents.title: Losing jobs summary for the owner meeting
paragraphs: Losing jobs summary of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month {col:tick_month.month}.

{col:tick_month.losing_jobs} of {col:tick_month.jobs} jobs lost money. Callbacks: {col:tick_month.cb_count} costing {col:tick_month.cb_cost}. Gross profit after callbacks: {col:tick_month.gross_profit}, which is {col:tick_month.margin_pct} of revenue.

Parts cost {col:tick_month.parts_cost}, labour cost {col:tick_month.labour_cost}, subcontract cost {col:tick_month.sub_cost}. Use the Losing-Money Job Finder for the job list and bring it to the meeting.
Decisions and owners are written below.

documents.title: Parts used on a job with cost against the book
paragraphs: Parts used note of {set:company}, dated {today}. Job {col:jobs.job_id} on {col:jobs.date}, {col:jobs.job_type}, van {col:jobs.van}, technician {col:jobs.technician}.
Parts cost entered {col:jobs.parts_cost}; parts cost in the price book {col:jobs.book_parts}; difference {col:jobs.parts_over}. Entry check: {col:jobs.entry_flag}.
Price of the job {col:jobs.price}. Check every part against the van stock count and the supplier invoice before the job is closed.
Initials and date are written below.

paragraphs: Subcontract cost record of {set:company}, dated {today}. Job {col:jobs.job_id} on {col:jobs.date}, site {col:jobs.site_ref}, {col:jobs.job_type}.
Subcontract cost {col:jobs.sub_cost}; permit fee {col:jobs.permit_fee}; disposal {col:jobs.disposal}. Total cost of the job {col:jobs.total_cost}; price {col:jobs.price}; margin {col:jobs.margin}.

paragraphs: Job profit summary of {set:company} for the accountant, dated {today}. Month {col:tick_month.month}.

Revenue {col:tick_month.revenue} from {col:tick_month.jobs} jobs. Parts {col:tick_month.parts_cost}, labour {col:tick_month.labour_cost}, subcontract {col:tick_month.sub_cost}, permit, disposal and vehicle {col:tick_month.other_cost}. Margin before callbacks {col:tick_month.margin}.

Callback cost {col:tick_month.cb_cost}, of which warranty cost {col:tick_month.warranty_cost}; warranty reserve for the month {col:tick_month.reserve}. Gross profit after callbacks {col:tick_month.gross_profit}.
